da-false-claim.evidence: atomic-lp-stability.md:9-12 'The Borromean braid (σ1σ2)^3 is the identity in the standard (degree-2) representation of H3(q).'
da-false-claim.notes: This load-bearing claim is asserted with no proof and is suspect: (σ1σ2)^3 is the full twist / generator of the center of B_3, and it is NOT generally the identity in the 2-dimensional irreducible Hecke representation (it acts as a nonzero scalar, a power of q). If it were literally the identity the 'change of annihilation ratio' mechanism (q^{-10}) would be undercut. The premise as stated is likely false; at minimum unproved and central.

Not vacuous in the ':True' sense, but the substantive proposition content is entirely deferred to two sorry theorems, so the verified part is near-content-free relative to the claim.

da-hidden-dof.evidence: atomic-lp-stability.md:11 ratio 0.537 (bare) and 0.352 = q^{-10} (dressed); 0.537 ≈ q0^{-5.96} (computed), not an obvious q-power.
da-hidden-dof.notes: The bare ratio 0.537 appears as a bare constant with no derivation shown; numerically it is ≈ q0^{-5.96}, i.e. not a clean q-power, so its origin (eigenvalue ratio of σ0 in the degree-2 rep?) is unstated. The exponent -10 in the dressed q^{-10} is likewise asserted. These look like inserted numbers rather than chain-derived quantities.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: atomic-lp-stability.md:12-13 'This changes the annihilation ratio from 0.537 (bare) to q^{-10}=0.352 (dressed). The original annihilator X* cannot satisfy the dressed condition, so the atom is stable.'
da-non-sequitur.notes: The inference 'the original X* fails the dressed condition ⟹ the atom is stable' is a non-sequitur: stability requires NO normalised annihilator exists (the dressed_is_lp_stable ∀-claim), not merely that the one bare annihilator X* fails. The argument only rules out a single candidate; the universal-nonexistence step is missing (and is exactly the sorry on lean:104-109).

da-physical-implausibility.evidence: atomic-lp-stability.md:1-13 frames bare hydrogen as needing 'B3 dressing (proton internal structure)' to be 'stable'.
da-physical-implausibility.notes: Physically the hydrogen atom's stability is not contingent on proton internal (Borromean) structure; the proton being composite does not 'stabilise the atom' in any standard sense. This is a model-internal notion of 'LP stability', but the prose phrasing invites a physics reading a domain expert would reject. Flag as warn since 'stable' is defined model-internally, not claimed as the physical binding.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: major-revision. referee_argument: 'The proposition asserts bare-H LP-instability and dressed-H stability as results, but both are sorry in the Lean (the file honestly says so), the only verified fact is 0.537≠0.352, and the central inference "X* fails the dressed condition, so the atom is stable" is a non-sequitur (ruling out one annihilator ≠ universal nonexistence). The pivotal premise "(σ1σ2)^3 is the identity in the degree-2 rep of H3(q)" is almost certainly false (it is the full twist, a nonzero scalar), and the bare ratio 0.537 has no shown derivation. Restate as a conjecture/conditional, fix or justify the (σ1σ2)^3 premise, and supply the universal-nonexistence argument before claiming stability.'
